title: Adaptive channel tail-clip + sequence-aware layer rescaler for mixed FP8/INT8 profiles
creator: Marco Chen
description:
Background: We observe intermittent token-level entropy spikes for certain heads in LLama/Mistral/Qwen when applying a mixed FP8/INT8 quantization pipeline. Initial calibration profiles that use global per-layer scales leave heavy-tailed activation distributions unaddressed; this produces generation instability and occasional hallucination regressions on a small but visible fraction of prompts.

Goal: Implement an adaptive per-channel tail-clipping step and a sequence-aware layer rescaler that integrates with the existing calibration harness. The feature should: (1) detect and clip extreme tail values per-channel using a robust quantile estimator; (2) compute a sequence-aware rescale that preserves early-token dynamics while limiting late-step drift; (3) emit calibration artifacts and eval metrics to validate no >0.5% degradation on benchmark SFT/QA suites and reduce token-level outlier events by >=60%.

Scope: Engineering work to modify the calibration pipeline, runtime hooks for runtime rescaler enforcement, unit/e2e tests across LLama/Mistral/Qwen model configs, and an evaluation sweep with the existing accuracy/regression harness. This is not a model retraining effort — changes are limited to quantization preprocessing and runtime scale adjustments.
acceptance_criteria: Per-channel tail-clipping integrated into calibration harness and configurable via profile flag (enabled=false by default)
Sequence-aware layer rescaler computed during calibration and available as a lightweight runtime correction with <3% latency overhead on p99 for typical batch sizes
Quant eval shows <=0.5% regression on asked benchmarks (SFT/QA) compared to baseline FP32 when using recommended profile
Outlier events (defined as activation > 6 sigma above median) reduced by >=60% across validation sets for affected models
PRs merged with unit tests + hardware smoke on GPU infra; rollout gated behind runtime-1.20 feature flag
implementation_steps: Design: finalize statistical estimator for per-channel tail clipping (trimmed-quantile + Hampel filter) and publish short spec
Calibration harness: add tail-clip stage that computes channel-level clipping thresholds and stores them in profile JSON
Layer rescaler: implement sequence-aware algorithm that weighs early-token statistics higher and produces a multiplicative correction per-layer per-head
Runtime: expose lightweight rescale correction path with a fallthrough to existing kernels; ensure no change for profiles without rescale entries
Evaluation: run automated sweep on SFT / QA / LLM-adapted benchmarks for LLama, Mistral, Qwen; measure generation quality, token entropy, perplexity, and outlier counts
Perf testing: measure p50/p95/p99 latency overhead on dedicated pools and ensure overhead <3% on p99
Safety: run fuzz/regression harness for adversarial prompts that previously triggered outlier spikes
Docs & Console: add profile schema docs and console toggle; include visualization of per-channel clipping distribution in calibration artifact UI
notes_and_tradeoffs: Aggressive tail clipping can suppress legitimate rare tokens in some domain models; will make flag opt-in by default and add recommended presets per-family
Sequence-aware rescale introduces a non-uniform correction across tokens — we prioritize preserving early-token dynamics at the possible cost of slightly more conservative late-token clipping
Runtime correction is implemented as multiplicative scaling to avoid kernel-level rewrites; if further perf needed we can push into compiled kernels later
Alternative approaches evaluated: activation-weighted quantization, per-head mixed-precision. Rejected for now due to model-agnostic deploy complexity and higher runtime cost
testing_plan: Unit tests for estimator math with synthetic heavy-tailed data
Integration test in calibration harness that verifies profile JSON contains clipping thresholds and rescale map
Hardware smoke tests on CUDA and ROCm in CI
Quant-regression sweep (automated) comparing generation outputs vs FP32 baseline across ~2k prompts
Monitor rollout: A/B on small % of traffic with automatic rollback if regression >0.8% on safety metrics
